title: Granular drift-detecting upgrade sweeper playbook for private control plane
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) control plane upgrades currently rely on staged traffic promotion and basic health gates (pod readiness, api liveness). We lack a lightweight automated post-upgrade "sweeper" that detects subtle state drift (Terraform drift, CRD schema drift, config-map divergence, leader flips, reconciliation stalls) and escalates or auto-rolls back affected cohorts.

Proposal: Implement a Granular Drift-Detecting Upgrade Sweeper: a small orchestration service + Terraform hooks that runs as part of the upgrade pipeline and during the first 48h after promotion. Responsibilities: 1) Run plan/diff fingerprints for IaC (Terraform) against promoted tenant stacks and surface Terraform drift deltas at resource-level. 2) Execute control-plane behavioral probes per-tenant: reconciliation latency, KV cache warmup success, control API latency p50/p95, synthetic request path correctness. 3) Compare metric deltas against baseline windows (pre-upgrade rolling baseline) and detect anomalies with threshold + trend heuristics. 4) When thresholds exceeded, automatically isolate cohort (traffic-slice) and either (a) trigger immediate rollback for high-severity infra drift or (b) create a remediation task and route traffic to fallback variant for medium severity. 5) Record detailed triage artifacts (Terraform plan snippets, last-applied manifests, pod events, stack traces) and attach to the incident in PagerDuty/Console.

Implementation overview: - Terraform: add optional module outputs and a small lifecycle metadata resource (module_version, commit_sha) so sweeper can correlate live resources with the promoted build. Add a small "sweeper_hook" provider that can run preflight/postflight plans and produce normalized diffs. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform-modules/tree/upgrade-hooks. - Sweeper service: lightweight Go binary, k8s-deployable, config-driven per-upgrade cohort sizes, uses job workers to run probes and Terraform plan/apply-dryrun via remote state. Exposes an API for the upgrade operator to query status and to run manual rechecks. - Health checks: composite checks that combine infra-drift score + behavioral delta score; scoring knobs are configurable per-tenant-class (enterprise vs dev). - Canary sweep strategy: instead of single canary, the sweeper performs a "sweep": N micro-canaries across AZs and tenant cohorts, exercises cold starts (KV cache), schema migrations (if present), and long-tail tokenization regressions for small sample prompts. - Observability: emit per-tenant check events into telemetry (metrics + traces) with labels: upgrade_id, cohort_id, tenant_id, module_version. Wire Console to show a dedicated "Upgrade Sweeper" dashboard with per-cohort timelines and actionable links.

Safety & guardrails: - Maximum parallel drifts processed to avoid noisy throttles. - A strict hard-fail threshold (e.g., reconciliation latency > 15s p95 or > 20% Terraform-resource-absent deltas) that triggers immediate rollback. - Manual approval step for clusters flagged as medium severity for 2+ checks. - Feature flag toggle per-customer (opt-in; default on for Redwood-managed Dedicated trials).

Why different from prior work: This ticket focuses on post-promotion drift detection and per-tenant sweep (micro-canaries) rather than only traffic promotion gating. It ties Terraform diffs to runtime behavioral probes and produces deterministic forensic artifacts for fast root cause.

Artifacts & links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Upgrade+Sweeper+Design - Terraform module prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform-modules/pull/512 - Sweeper service prototype (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/tree/feature/sweeper - Dashboard mock: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/upgrade-sweeper-mock - Staging runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xUPg-staging-runbook
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose module_version and commit_sha metadata and pass integration tests (CI) when running plan against staging state
Sweeper service can run a sweep against a staging cohort and produce per-tenant reports (JSON + compressed logs) stored in s3 staging bucket
Console dashboard shows per-cohort timelines with links to Terraform diff snippets and trace IDs
Automated rollback triggers when hard-fail threshold is crossed during a sweep in staging (validated in two staging runs)
Security review completed for the sweeper service (KMS use for remote state creds and no persistent secret material in logs)
Runbook updated and on-call trained; one simulated rollback executed end-to-end during the QA week

2026-03-12 - Rohan Patel: updated probe runner to perform KV cache warmup (cold path) during sweep; saw a 12% increase in p95 for warmup in one staging tenant - investigating root cause with runtime team (ENG-704002 tentative dependency).

release_notes: Adds Upgrade Sweeper: post-promotion drift detection, per-tenant micro-canary sweeps, Terraform diff correlation, and automated rollback logic. Initially gated behind feature flag for Dedicated/private deployments.
